_comment: T-0075: a declarative weapon/spell spec, the Godot-side equivalent of watoom-unreal-combat's combat_spec.zas.json, loaded by `gg_combat.py spec --spec <this file> --weapon|--spell NAME` and (for just the vfx half) `gg_vfx.py check --combat-spec <this file>`. effect.damage_type is the resist lookup key on CombatAttributes.resist -- game/combat.gd calls it damage_type, not 'element'; this doc's own prose still says 'element' informally since that is what the ticket and the Unreal side call the same concept. 'low-poly-weapons-set-0794c54e' is a real owned pack (StaticMesh-only: assault rifle/shotgun/pistol props, no skeleton/animation), exported via the unreal-export bridge on 2026-11-18 (PORTABLE_EXPORT_PASS, 8/8 StaticMesh, 0 failed) -- converted to glb with blender-export-pipelines fbx_relink_to_glb.py into the pack's glb/converted/ (indexed), brought into a project with `gg_assets.py use --asset low-poly-weapons-set-0794c54e-sm-assaultrifle-01 --slot ar_body` (and -magazine-01 ar_mag, -trigger-01 ar_trigger, sm-pumpshotgun-01 sg_body, sm-pumpshotgun-trigger-01 sg_trigger). 'mesh' is the body glb, 'parts' the separately exported pieces on the same pivot; `gg_combat.py spec` checks the body's size and that each part sits on it.
